card.name: Words leading into a harmful outcome
card.fires_on: Small linking words or verbs such as 'for', 'in', 'of', 'and', 'leading' and 'faces' that come right before a named problem, side effect or lab abnormality. They are most common in drug interaction text, e.g. before hypokalemia or hyperkalemia.

modes.label: Link before a lab abnormality
modes.description: A preposition after risk, result or observed closely, just before a low or high electrolyte term.

modes.label: Verb of facing trouble
modes.description: A verb like faces or leading that introduces a looming problem.
modes.example: Increased exposure of citalopram<< leading>> to an increased risk of QT prolongation

modes.label: Heading link
modes.description: The word and inside a Warnings and Precautions heading reference.
